questions.stem: The LONGEST MOUNTAIN RANGE on Earth (above water) is the:

options.option_text: ANDES of South America (~7,000 km) — longest continental range running along 7 countries from Venezuela to Argentina

questions.explanation: LONGEST CONTINENTAL MOUNTAIN RANGE — the ANDES (~7,000 km / 4,300 mi) along WEST coast of SOUTH AMERICA; passes through 7 countries (from north to south): VENEZUELA, COLOMBIA, ECUADOR, PERU, BOLIVIA, CHILE, ARGENTINA. Formed by SUBDUCTION of the NAZCA plate beneath the SOUTH AMERICAN plate. HIGHEST peak: ACONCAGUA (Argentina, 6,961 m) — also highest peak OUTSIDE Asia; LOCATION of high-altitude civilisations (Inca, capital Cusco at 3,400 m); LAKE TITICACA (Bolivia-Peru border at 3,812 m — highest navigable lake). Passes: include ATACAMA DESERT (driest on Earth) to the west. NOTE: Technically the LONGEST MOUNTAIN RANGE on Earth is the MID-OCEANIC RIDGE (~65,000 km, mostly UNDERWATER); but the question specifies 'above water' / continental. HIMALAYAS (~2,400 km) — highest, not longest. ROCKIES of North America (~4,800 km, USA-Canada) — second-longest continental. Other major ranges: ALPS (Europe, 1,200 km), URALS (Russia, 2,500 km — divides Europe & Asia), ATLAS (Africa), SIERRA MADRE (Mexico), DRAKENSBERG (S. Africa), GREAT DIVIDING RANGE (Australia).

questions.stem: The DEEPEST point in the world's oceans is CHALLENGER DEEP, located in the:

options.option_text: MARIANA TRENCH in the Pacific Ocean — ~10,984 m (36,037 ft) deep; east of the Mariana Islands near Guam

questions.explanation: MARIANA TRENCH — crescent-shaped depression in the WESTERN PACIFIC OCEAN; east of the MARIANA ISLANDS (near Guam); ~2,550 km long, ~69 km wide. DEEPEST POINT: CHALLENGER DEEP (southern end), measured ~10,984 m (36,037 ft) below sea level — deeper than Mount Everest (8,849 m) is tall. If you put Everest at its bottom, it would still be submerged by >2 km of water. NAMED after the British Royal Navy ship HMS CHALLENGER (1872-76 expedition, first sounded the depth at 8,184 m — far short of actual). FORMED by subduction of the PACIFIC PLATE beneath the PHILIPPINE plate. FIRST MANNED DESCENT: JACQUES PICCARD (Swiss) and DON WALSH (US Navy) in 1960 aboard the bathyscaphe TRIESTE — reached 10,911 m. 2012: JAMES CAMERON (filmmaker) solo descent in DEEPSEA CHALLENGER submersible. 2019: VICTOR VESCOVO in LIMITING FACTOR — recorded 10,927 m. Temperature near bottom: ~1-4°C. Pressure: 1086 bars (~1072 atm) — over 1000 times surface atmospheric pressure. Life exists even here — microbes, amphipods, snailfish. OTHER DEEP TRENCHES: Tonga Trench (10,882 m), Philippine Trench (10,540 m), Kuril-Kamchatka, Kermadec, Puerto Rico (Atlantic, 8,376 m — deepest of Atlantic), Java/Sunda (Indian Ocean, 7,290 m — deepest of Indian).

questions.stem: The LARGEST DESERT in the world (by area) is the:

options.option_text: Sahara Desert (~9.2 million sq km, North Africa)
ANTARCTIC DESERT (~14.2 million sq km) — cold desert; a ‘desert’ is defined by low precipitation (<250 mm/year), not by heat
Gobi Desert (~1.3 million sq km, Mongolia-China)

questions.explanation: BY SCIENTIFIC DEFINITION — a ‘desert’ is an area receiving LESS THAN 250 mm (10 in) of annual precipitation, NOT necessarily hot. By that metric: LARGEST DESERT on Earth = ANTARCTIC POLAR DESERT, ~14.2 MILLION sq km (5.5 million sq mi); covers the entire continent of Antarctica; receives only 50-200 mm equivalent precipitation as snow per year. 2nd-largest: ARCTIC DESERT (~13.7 million sq km). 3rd: SAHARA (~9.2 million sq km, NORTH AFRICA — largest HOT desert). RANKING of large HOT deserts: SAHARA > ARABIAN (2.3M, Arabian peninsula) > GOBI (1.3M, Mongolia-China) > KALAHARI (0.93M, Southern Africa) > PATAGONIAN (0.67M, Argentina-Chile) > GREAT VICTORIA (0.65M, Australia) > GREAT BASIN (0.49M, USA) > SYRIAN > CHIHUAHUAN > THAR (Great Indian, 0.2M — India-Pakistan). INDIA’S THAR covers W Rajasthan, parts of Gujarat, and across border into Sindh, Pakistan — 7th-largest SUBTROPICAL desert. DRIEST place on Earth (lowest recorded precipitation): ATACAMA DESERT (northern Chile) — some regions haven’t received rain in 400+ years; cold-current effect from Humboldt current. HOTTEST (record): FURNACE CREEK, DEATH VALLEY (California) — 56.7°C (10 July 1913, disputed); LUT DESERT (Iran) — surface temp 70.7°C by satellite.

questions.stem: The LONGEST RIVER in the world is (by most modern measurements):

options.option_text: Amazon (~6,400 km — disputed in recent studies)
NILE (~6,650 km, Africa) — traditional ranking; flows N through 11 countries into the Mediterranean Sea; some 2023 studies suggest Amazon may be slightly longer

questions.explanation: NILE — traditionally considered LONGEST river; ~6,650 km from its deepest source (LAKE VICTORIA, or further tributaries in RWANDA / BURUNDI / ETHIOPIA highlands) to the MEDITERRANEAN Sea delta in EGYPT. Flows NORTH through 11 countries: BURUNDI, RWANDA, TANZANIA, UGANDA, DR CONGO, KENYA, ETHIOPIA, SOUTH SUDAN, SUDAN, EGYPT, ERITREA (basin). Two MAJOR TRIBUTARIES: (1) WHITE NILE — source Lake Victoria; longer, colder; (2) BLUE NILE — source Lake Tana (Ethiopia); supplies ~85% of water + silt during floods; the two meet at KHARTOUM (Sudan). Gives rise to ancient Egyptian civilisation; ASWAN HIGH DAM (1970) built on it; creates LAKE NASSER. 2007 & 2023 studies using GPS and satellite re-measurement suggest the AMAZON (Peru to Atlantic, Brazil) may be ~6,992 km, slightly LONGER than Nile — so the question is increasingly contested. AMAZON is undisputedly: (1) LARGEST BY DISCHARGE (Volume) — 209,000 m³/s, nearly 5x Congo (next biggest); (2) largest DRAINAGE BASIN (~7 million sq km); (3) widest river. OTHER TOP RIVERS: YANGTZE (6,300 km, longest in Asia, China), MISSISSIPPI-MISSOURI (USA), YENISEI (Russia), YELLOW / HUANG HE (China), OB (Russia), PARANA (S America), CONGO (2nd by discharge), AMUR (Russia-China), LENA (Russia).

questions.stem: Which is the LARGEST FRESHWATER lake in the world by area?

options.option_text: Lake Baikal (Siberia, Russia) — largest by VOLUME, deepest in the world
LAKE SUPERIOR (Great Lakes, USA-Canada border) — 82,100 sq km — largest FRESHWATER lake by SURFACE AREA

questions.explanation: LAKE SUPERIOR — largest FRESHWATER LAKE in the world BY AREA (82,100 sq km); one of 5 GREAT LAKES (SUPERIOR, MICHIGAN, HURON, ERIE, ONTARIO — mnemonic ‘SMHEO’ or ‘HOMES’); bordered by CANADA (Ontario) to the north and USA (Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan) to the south. CASPIAN SEA (371,000 sq km) is LARGER but is a SALTWATER endorheic ‘sea’ (saline); technically the world's largest inland BODY of water. Among freshwater by surface area: SUPERIOR > VICTORIA (Africa, 68,800 — largest IN AFRICA, 3rd-largest world freshwater) > HURON > MICHIGAN > TANGANYIKA (E. Africa, 2nd-largest by volume, deepest in Africa 1,470 m). By VOLUME: (1) CASPIAN (saline); by FRESHWATER volume: (1) BAIKAL (Russia/Siberia) — holds 22-23% of world's freshwater, 1,642 m deep (deepest in world, OLDEST at 25-30 million years, UNESCO WHS); (2) TANGANYIKA; (3) SUPERIOR. DEEPEST: BAIKAL (1,642 m). HIGHEST navigable: TITICACA (Bolivia-Peru border, 3,812 m). LOWEST ELEVATION lake: DEAD SEA (-430 m below sea level, 34% salinity — one of saltiest). LARGEST IN INDIA: WULAR (J&K, freshwater, tectonic); LARGEST SALTWATER in India: CHILIKA (Odisha, brackish). LARGEST ARTIFICIAL LAKE: KARIBA (Zimbabwe-Zambia).

questions.stem: The EQUATOR passes through the LARGEST NUMBER OF COUNTRIES on which continent?

options.option_text: AFRICA — equator passes through 7 African countries (São Tomé & Príncipe, Gabon, Republic of Congo, DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya, Somalia)
South America (passes through Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil)

questions.explanation: EQUATOR (0° latitude) — passes through 13 COUNTRIES in total globally. AFRICA has the MOST — 7 countries: (1) SÃO TOMÉ & PRÍNCIPE (island, off W. Africa), (2) GABON, (3) REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO, (4) DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO (DRC), (5) UGANDA, (6) KENYA, (7) SOMALIA (through territorial waters). SOUTH AMERICA: 3 countries — ECUADOR (named after equator!), COLOMBIA, BRAZIL. ASIA: 2 countries — INDONESIA (passes through Borneo/Kalimantan, Sumatra), MALDIVES (small islands straddle). OCEANIA: 1 — KIRIBATI (passes through some islands). TOTAL: 7+3+2+1 = 13. TROPIC OF CANCER (23.5° N) — passes through MEXICO, BAHAMAS, WESTERN SAHARA, MAURITANIA, MALI, ALGERIA, NIGER, LIBYA, EGYPT, SAUDI ARABIA, UAE, OMAN, INDIA (8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram), BANGLADESH, MYANMAR, CHINA, TAIWAN. In INDIA, Tropic of Cancer is a useful mnemonic for ‘8 states through which it passes’. TROPIC OF CAPRICORN (23.5° S) — passes through AUSTRALIA, CHILE, ARGENTINA, PARAGUAY, BRAZIL, NAMIBIA, BOTSWANA, S. AFRICA, MOZAMBIQUE, MADAGASCAR. INTERNATIONAL DATE LINE roughly follows 180° meridian through the Pacific, deviating to avoid landmasses.

questions.stem: Which ocean is the SMALLEST and SHALLOWEST of the world's five oceans?
questions.explanation: ARCTIC OCEAN — SMALLEST and SHALLOWEST of the world's 5 oceans. DIMENSIONS: Surface area ~14.06 million sq km (vs Pacific 165 M); avg depth ~1,200 m (vs Pacific avg 4,280 m). BORDERED BY 8 ARCTIC COUNTRIES: USA (Alaska), Canada, Denmark (Greenland), Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Russia. FEATURES: (1) largely COVERED by SEA ICE year-round (shrinking due to climate change — Arctic sea ice minimum in September each year); (2) the NORTH POLE sits in its centre, on floating ice, not land; (3) contains the NORTH GEOGRAPHIC POLE; (4) home to Inuit, polar bears, seals, walruses, whales. WORLD’S 5 OCEANS (by size, LARGEST → SMALLEST): (1) PACIFIC (~165.25M sq km, nearly 1/3 of Earth) — DEEPEST; contains Mariana Trench; (2) ATLANTIC (~106.46M) — S-shaped; contains Puerto Rico Trench; Sargasso Sea; (3) INDIAN (~70.56M); warmest; contains Java Trench; (4) SOUTHERN / ANTARCTIC (~20.33M) — surrounds Antarctica up to 60°S (recognised as distinct 5th ocean by IHO 2000, by National Geographic 2021); contains Antarctic Circumpolar Current (largest ocean current); (5) ARCTIC (~14.06M) — smallest, shallowest, coldest. All connect — one world ocean. COVER ~71% of Earth's surface. ~14.06 million sq km; bordered by 8 countries; partly ice-covered year-round; avg depth ~1,200 m.

questions.stem: The GREAT BARRIER REEF, the world's largest coral reef system, is located off the coast of:
questions.explanation: GREAT BARRIER REEF — World's LARGEST coral reef system; stretches ~2,300 km (1,400 mi) along the north-eastern coast of AUSTRALIA (mostly off the coast of QUEENSLAND), in the CORAL SEA (western Pacific). COMPRISES 2,900+ individual reefs, 900+ islands. VISIBLE FROM SPACE — the largest structure built by living organisms on Earth. HOME TO: 1,500 fish species, 411 coral types, 134 sharks/rays, dugongs, humpback whales, 6 turtle species. UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE (1981). THREATS: coral bleaching (due to ocean warming), agri runoff, crown-of-thorns starfish — multiple mass bleaching events in 2016, 2017, 2020, 2022, 2024. OTHER MAJOR REEFS: (1) BELIZE BARRIER REEF (Central America, 2nd largest, UNESCO); (2) NEW CALEDONIA BARRIER REEF (Pacific, 3rd); (3) RED SEA reefs; (4) INDIAN REEFS — LAKSHADWEEP (atolls, only coral atolls of India), GULF OF MANNAR, GULF OF KUTCH, ANDAMAN & NICOBAR, MALVAN (Maharashtra). CORAL REEFS form in shallow (<100 m) warm (20-28°C) tropical seas; need sunlight (zooxanthellae photosynthesis). Types: FRINGING (close to shore), BARRIER (separated by lagoon), ATOLL (ring-shaped, around submerged volcano island — e.g. Lakshadweep, Maldives). stretches ~2,300 km; visible from space; UNESCO site 1981; in the Coral Sea.

questions.stem: The ‘Ring of Fire’, a belt known for intense volcanic and seismic activity, is associated with the:
questions.explanation: PACIFIC RING OF FIRE (also ‘Circum-Pacific Belt’) — a horseshoe-shaped ZONE, ~40,000 km in length, encircling the PACIFIC OCEAN; characterised by intense TECTONIC activity: (1) ~75% of world’s ACTIVE (and dormant) VOLCANOES — ~450 of 850; (2) ~90% of world’s EARTHQUAKES; (3) the world’s largest earthquakes happen here — e.g., Chile 1960 (M 9.5, largest ever recorded), Alaska 1964 (M 9.2), Sumatra 2004 (M 9.1, caused Indian Ocean tsunami), Japan Tōhoku 2011 (M 9.1). CAUSED BY: numerous SUBDUCTION zones — Pacific plate, Nazca plate, Cocos plate, Juan de Fuca, Philippine, Indo-Australian plates — all dive beneath continental plates, creating trenches + arcs of volcanoes + frequent seismicity. COUNTRIES ON THE RING: New Zealand, Tonga, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia, Philippines, Taiwan, Japan, Russia (Kamchatka), Aleutian Islands (USA), Alaska (USA), western Canada, western USA (California), Mexico, Guatemala, Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Chile. Famous volcanoes on the Ring: FUJI (Japan), PINATUBO (Philippines, erupted 1991), KRAKATOA (Indonesia, 1883), MERAPI (Indonesia), MT. ST. HELENS (USA, 1980), POPOCATÉPETL (Mexico), COTOPAXI (Ecuador), MAUNA LOA (Hawaii). SECONDARY BELT: the ALPINE-HIMALAYAN / MEDITERRANEAN belt (~17% of earthquakes) — includes Himalayas, Iran, Turkey, Italy (Mt Etna, Vesuvius). a horseshoe-shaped belt around the Pacific where ~75% of world's active volcanoes and ~90% of earthquakes occur, due to subduction at plate margins.

questions.stem: The ANGEL FALLS, the highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world, is located in:

options.option_text: VENEZUELA — in Canaima National Park; 979 m (3,212 ft) total drop; named after US pilot Jimmie Angel (1933)

questions.explanation: ANGEL FALLS (Spanish: ‘Salto Ángel’; indigenous Pemon: ‘KEREPAKUPAI MERÚ’ = ‘Waterfall of the Deepest Place’) — HIGHEST UNINTERRUPTED WATERFALL in the world. TOTAL HEIGHT: 979 m (3,212 ft); uninterrupted single drop: 807 m (2,648 ft). LOCATION: AUYÁN-TEPUI mountain, CANAIMA NATIONAL PARK (UNESCO World Heritage), BOLÍVAR STATE, VENEZUELA. Named after JIMMIE ANGEL, the American aviator who first flew over them in 1933 and crash-landed on top in 1937. The water plunges from a flat-topped TEPUI mountain into a gorge. The falls inspired ‘Paradise Falls’ in the animated film UP (Pixar, 2009). OTHER WATERFALLS of note: (1) VICTORIA FALLS (Mosi-oa-Tunya = ‘smoke that thunders’) — Zambia/Zimbabwe border, 108 m high but WIDEST curtain at 1,708 m, explorer David Livingstone named it 1855; (2) NIAGARA FALLS — USA/Canada, 51 m, but highest WATER VOLUME; (3) IGUAZU FALLS — Brazil/Argentina, 82 m, 275 cascades, ‘Niagara on steroids’; (4) TUGELA FALLS — South Africa, 948 m (some argue highest if cascaded drops counted). INDIA’S HIGHEST WATERFALLS: KUNCHIKAL (Karnataka, 455 m, tallest in India), JOG (Karnataka, 253 m), DUDHSAGAR (Goa-Karnataka border, 310 m).
